subject: Quantitative Ability
q: By how many degrees does the sum of the interior angles of a 10-sided polygon exceed that of a 6-sided polygon?
explanation: Each extra side adds 180°: (10 − 6) × 180° = 720°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with 12 sides?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = ∠C, ∠B = 100° and ∠D = 112°. What is ∠A?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 108°. What is the total of all its interior angles?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 135°. How many sides does it have?
explanation: Exterior angle = 180 − 135 = 45°; sides = 360 ÷ 45 = 8.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A regular polygon has interior angles of 150° each. Which polygon is it?
explanation: Exterior angle = 180 − 150 = 30°; 360 ÷ 30 = 12 sides, a dodecagon.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 120° more than its exterior angle. How many sides does it have?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If each angle of a regular polygon is 150°, how many vertices does it have?
explanation: Exterior angle = 180 − 150 = 30°; a polygon has as many vertices as sides: 360 ÷ 30 = 12.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a regular polygon the ratio of an interior angle to an exterior angle is 5 : 1. How many sides does the polygon have?
explanation: Interior = 5 × exterior and interior + exterior = 180°, so exterior = 180 ÷ 6 = 30°; sides = 360 ÷ 30 = 12.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is one-third of its interior angle. How many sides does it have?
explanation: Interior = 3 × exterior and interior + exterior = 180°, so exterior = 180 ÷ 4 = 45°; sides = 360 ÷ 45 = 8.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is one-fifth of a right angle. How many sides does it have?
explanation: Exterior angle = 90° ÷ 5 = 18°; sides = 360 ÷ 18 = 20.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 4 times the sum of its exterior angles. How many sides does it have?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two angles of a triangle are 70° and 49°. What is the third angle?
explanation: Angles of a triangle add up to 180°: 180 − 70 − 49 = 61°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5. What is the largest angle?
explanation: 9 parts = 180°, so one part = 20°; the largest angle is 5 × 20 = 100°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a right-angled triangle one of the acute angles is 67°. What is the other acute angle?
explanation: The acute angles of a right-angled triangle add up to 90°: 90 − 67 = 23°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The angles of a triangle are x°, 5x° and 4x°. What is the value of x?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In triangle ABC, ∠A is 28° more than ∠B and ∠C = 88°. Find ∠A.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The angles of a triangle are (x + 7)°, (2x − 4)° and (x + 33)°. What is the value of x?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a triangle, the largest angle is five times the smallest, and the third angle is 66°. What is the largest angle?
explanation: smallest + 5 × smallest = 180 − 66 = 114°, so the smallest is 19° and the largest 95°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Which of the following sets of angles could be the angles of a triangle?
explanation: Only 51°, 84°, 45° add up to 180° (51 + 84 + 45); the other sets total 190°, 195°, 165°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The two acute angles of a right-angled triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the smaller of them?
explanation: The acute angles total 90°: 5 parts = 90°, one part = 18°, so the smaller is 36°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two angles of a triangle add up to 149° and differ by 25°. What is the largest angle of the triangle?
explanation: The two angles are (149 + 25) ÷ 2 = 87° and 62°; the third is 180 − 149 = 31°. The largest is 87°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two angles of a triangle are each 67°. What is the third angle?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: One angle of a triangle is half of the sum of the other two angles. What is that angle?
explanation: If the angle is x, the other two total 2x, so x + 2x = 180 and x = 60°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The two equal angles of an isosceles triangle are 26° each. What is the third angle?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle is 36°. What is each base angle?
explanation: The base angles are equal: (180 − 36) ÷ 2 = 72°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: One angle of an isosceles triangle is 98°. What are the other two angles?
explanation: An obtuse angle can only be the vertex angle (two obtuse angles would exceed 180°), so the other two are (180 − 98) ÷ 2 = 41° each.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: One angle of an isosceles triangle is 78°. Which of the following could be another of its angles?
explanation: If 78° is a base angle, the angles are 78°, 78°, 24°; if it is the vertex angle, the others are 51° each. So 51° is possible; the other options fit neither case.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In an isosceles triangle each base angle is 7 times the vertex angle. What is the vertex angle?
explanation: If the vertex angle is v, each base angle is 7v, so v + 14v = 180 and v = 12°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle is 30° more than each base angle. Find the vertex angle.
explanation: Base angles b, vertex b + 30: 3b + 30 = 180, so b = 50° and the vertex angle is 80°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In triangle PQR, PQ = PR and ∠Q = 58°. What is ∠P?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In an isosceles right-angled triangle, each of the two equal angles measures:
explanation: The right angle is the vertex angle; the other two are equal and share 90°, so each is 45°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In triangle ABC, AB = AC. Side BC is extended beyond C, and the exterior angle formed at C is 107°. What is ∠A?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 102°. What is the difference between a base angle and the vertex angle?
explanation: Each base angle is (180 − 102) ÷ 2 = 39°; the difference from 102° is 63°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 82° and one of the interior opposite angles is 31°. What is the other interior opposite angle?
explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles: 82 − 31 = 51°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 102° and the interior opposite angles are in the ratio 1 : 2. The interior opposite angles measure:
explanation: The two interior opposite angles add up to 102°; 3 parts = 102°, so they are 34° and 68°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 76°. What is the interior angle adjacent to it?
explanation: An exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a straight line: 180 − 76 = 104°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In triangle ABC, side BC is extended to D. If ∠ACD = 98° and ∠A = 20°, find ∠B.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In triangle ABC, BC is produced to D so that ∠ACD = 144°. If ∠A = ∠B, find ∠A.
explanation: ∠A + ∠B = ∠ACD = 144°; with ∠A = ∠B, each is 72°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The exterior angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the smallest interior angle?
explanation: Exterior angles total 360°: they are 80°, 120°, 160°. The smallest interior angle is 180 − 160 = 20°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 120°, and the two interior opposite angles differ by 10°. What is the larger of them?
explanation: The two angles add up to 120° and differ by 10°, so the larger is (120 + 10) ÷ 2 = 65°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The interior angles of a triangle are 20°, 75° and 85°. What is its largest exterior angle?
explanation: The largest exterior angle is next to the smallest interior angle: 180 − 20 = 160°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In triangle PQR, ∠P = x°, ∠Q = (x + 18)° and the exterior angle at R is 122°. Find x.
explanation: The exterior angle at R equals ∠P + ∠Q: x + (x + 18) = 122, so 2x = 104 and x = 52.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 5 times the interior angle next to it. What is that interior angle?
explanation: interior + 5 × interior = 180°, so the interior angle is 180 ÷ 6 = 30°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the complement of an angle of 43°?
explanation: Complementary angles add up to 90°: 90 − 43 = 47°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the supplement of an angle of 41°?
explanation: Supplementary angles add up to 180°: 180 − 41 = 139°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the measure of an angle that is equal to its own complement?
explanation: If x = 90 − x, then 2x = 90 and x = 45°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An angle is 9 times its complement. Find the angle.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An angle is 120° more than its supplement. What is the angle?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The supplement of an angle is 6 times its complement. What is the angle?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two complementary angles are in the ratio 2 : 7. What is the larger angle?
explanation: 9 parts = 90°, so one part = 10° and the larger angle is 7 × 10 = 70°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two supplementary angles differ by 66°. What is the smaller angle?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: By how much does the supplement of 53° exceed its complement?
explanation: (180 − 53) − (90 − 53) = 90°; the difference is always 90°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Find the angle whose supplement is 9 times the angle itself.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One of a pair of corresponding angles is 61°. What is the other?
explanation: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so the other angle is also 61°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. If one of a pair of co-interior angles is 36°, what is the other?
explanation: Co-interior (allied) angles add up to 180°: 180 − 36 = 144°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, one of a pair of alternate interior angles is 122°. The other angle of the pair is:
explanation: Alternate interior angles formed by a transversal across parallel lines are equal: 122°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A transversal cuts two parallel lines, making co-interior angles of (2x + 14)° and (4x − 74)°. What is x?
explanation: Co-interior angles add up to 180°: 6x  − 60 = 180, so x = 40.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two alternate angles formed by a transversal across parallel lines are (4x − 54)° and (2x + 6)°. Find x.
explanation: Alternate angles are equal: 4x − 54 = 2x + 6, so 2x = 60 and x = 30.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal across two parallel lines are (4x − 98)° and (x + 19)°. What is the size of each angle?
explanation: Corresponding angles are equal: 4x − 98 = x + 19 gives x = 39, so each angle is 58°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A transversal meets two parallel lines, and one of the eight angles formed is 84°. What is the sum of all the obtuse angles formed?
explanation: The eight angles are four of 84° and four of 96°; the obtuse ones total 4 × 96 = 384°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two co-interior angles between a pair of parallel lines are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the smaller angle?
explanation: Co-interior angles total 180°: 5 parts = 180°, so the smaller is 2 × 36 = 72°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle are 15 cm and 20 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 29 cm and one of the other sides is 20 cm. Find the third side.
explanation: 29² − 20² = 841 − 400 = 441, so the third side is 21 cm.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A ladder 10 m long rests against a vertical wall with its foot 6 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
explanation: height² = 10² − 6² = 64, so the height is 8 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the length of the diagonal of a rectangle measuring 7 cm by 24 cm?
explanation: diagonal² = 7² + 24² = 625, so the diagonal is 25 cm.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A man walks 18 km due north and then 80 km due east. How far is he from his starting point?
explanation: The paths are at right angles: √(18² + 80²) = √6724 = 82 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Which of the following sets of lengths can form a right-angled triangle?
explanation: 15² + 20² = 625 = 25², so 15, 20, 25 is a right-angled triangle; the other sets fail this test.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The diagonal of a square is 21√2 cm. What is the length of its side?
explanation: A square of side s has diagonal s√2, so s = 21 cm.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A kite string 41 m long is pulled tight and tied to the ground. The kite is directly above a point 9 m from where the string is tied. How high is the kite?
explanation: The string is the hypotenuse: height² = 41² − 9² = 1600, so the kite is 40 m high.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 18 cm and 24 cm long. What is the length of each side?
explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, giving half-diagonals 9 and 12; side = √(81 + 144) = 15 cm.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of 50 cm and a base of 60 cm. What is its height?
explanation: The height bisects the base: height² = 50² − 30² = 1600, so the height is 40 cm.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 60 cm and a perimeter of 144 cm. What is its area?
explanation: a + b = 84 and a² + b² = 3600; 2ab = 7056 − 3600 = 3456, so the area ab/2 = 864 cm².

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two vertical poles 41 m and 5 m high stand 48 m apart on level ground. What is the distance between their tops?
explanation: The height difference is 41 − 5 = 36 m and the gap 48 m: distance = √(1296 + 2304) = 60 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A ship sails 5 km west from a port and then 12 km south. How far is it from the port in a straight line?
explanation: Distance = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The sides of a right-angled triangle are x, x + 1 and x + 2, the last being the hypotenuse. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
explanation: x² + (x + 1)² = (x + 2)² is satisfied by x = 3: 9 + 16 = 25. The hypotenuse is 5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the size of an angle in a semicircle?
explanation: An angle inscribed in a semicircle (standing on a diameter) is always a right angle.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An arc subtends an angle of 150° at the centre of a circle. What angle does it subtend at a point on the remaining part of the circle?
explanation: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre: 150 ÷ 2 = 75°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A chord subtends an angle of 30° at a point on the major arc of a circle. What angle does it subtend at the centre?
explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference: 2 × 30 = 60°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: From an external point P, a tangent PT touches a circle with centre O at T. If ∠TPO = 47°, what is ∠TOP?
explanation: The radius OT is perpendicular to the tangent, so ∠OTP = 90° and ∠TOP = 180 − 90 − 47 = 43°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: One angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is 142°. What is the angle opposite to it?
explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°: 180 − 142 = 38°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is another point on the circle. If ∠CAB = 57°, find ∠CBA.
explanation: ∠ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle), so ∠CBA = 180 − 90 − 57 = 33°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two radii of a circle make an angle of 72° at the centre. What is each of the other two angles of the triangle formed by the radii and the chord joining their ends?
explanation: The two radii are equal, so the triangle is isosceles: (180 − 72) ÷ 2 = 54° each.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are (3x + 14)° and (x + 102)°. Find x.
explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: 4x + 116 = 180, so x = 16.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: How many diagonals does a nonagon have?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A polygon has 20 diagonals. How many sides does it have?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: How many diagonals can be drawn from one vertex of a 9-sided polygon?
explanation: From one vertex you cannot draw a diagonal to itself or its two neighbours: 9 − 3 = 6.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The diagonals drawn from one vertex divide a pentagon into how many triangles?
explanation: The diagonals from one vertex split an n-gon into n − 2 triangles: 5 − 2 = 3.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: How many more diagonals does a 15-sided polygon have than an 11-sided polygon?
explanation: 15-gon: 90 diagonals; 11-gon: 44; difference 46.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A regular polygon has interior angles of 160° each. How many diagonals does it have?
explanation: Exterior angle = 180 − 160 = 20°, so n = 18; diagonals = 18 × 15 ÷ 2 = 135.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Three angles on a straight line are 4x°, 5x° and 9x°. Find x.
explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: 18x = 180, so x = 10.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Four angles meet at a point: 93°, 103°, 65° and x°. Find x.
explanation: Angles at a point add up to 360°: 360 − (93 + 103 + 65) = 99°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two straight lines intersect, and one of the four angles formed is 128°. What is the sum of the two angles next to it?
explanation: Each angle adjacent to 128° is 180 − 128 = 52°; the two together make 104°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: When two straight lines intersect, one angle is 8 times an angle adjacent to it. What is the smaller angle?
explanation: Adjacent angles at an intersection add up to 180°: s + 8s = 180, so s = 20°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Four angles at a point are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 : 8. What is the largest angle?
explanation: 18 parts = 360°, so one part = 20° and the largest angle is 8 × 20 = 160°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Three angles on a straight line are (x + 6)°, (2x − 21)° and 51°. Find x.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the reflex angle that goes with an angle of 132°?
explanation: The reflex angle is 360° − 132° = 228°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two vertically opposite angles are (3x − 12)° and (x + 8)°. What is x?
explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal: 3x − 12 = x + 8, so 2x = 20 and x = 10.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Four angles around a point are x°, (x + 10)°, (x + 20)° and (x + 30)°. What is the largest of them?
explanation: 4x + 60 = 360, so x = 75°; the largest is x + 30 = 105°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two straight lines intersect, and three of the four angles formed add up to 261°. What is the smallest of the four angles?
explanation: The fourth angle is 360 − 261 = 99°. Its neighbours are 180 − 99 = 81°, so the smallest angle is 81°.
